text:
leo-cust-sre: heads up — acme-corp reporting p95 jump from 120ms -> 900ms for /v1/generate since 02:05UTC, started after their spike of varied prompt prefixes. looks like KV prefix cache miss rate spiked to ~87% :grimacing:
jasmin-support: logged ticket #INC-3489, customer reports latency also affecting embedding calls. they saw lots of different headers on requests (x-client-version, x-feature-flags).
leo-cust-sre: attaching quick metrics: kv_hit_rate: 0.13; prefix_warmup_latency_p95: 340ms; node_cpu slightly high on hosts serving tenant.
tara-eng-runtime: thanks. can you paste a sample request header set? suspect header-key explosion creating unique cache keys (we saw similar with noisy user-agent before).
leo-cust-sre: sample: `{"x-client-version":"1.4.2-beta-7","x-feature-flags":"alpha:1,beta:0,gamma:42","session-id":"s-...","x-ab-test":"treatment-b"}` — client libs are sending flags in header not normalized.
mike-sre: if headers are included in prefix key, that would massively increase key cardinality. recommend short-term mitigation: drop noisy headers from cache key for this route and increase prefix TTL to 30s to allow warmup. can we toggle via route override? @deploy-bot any quick rollback?
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline status: can apply route override to remove header hashing for route `acme-corp/*` with a config change. 2-step: create override -> canary -> full. estimated 8m to canary.
jasmin-support: customer ok with scheduled 10m mitigation now. want to minimize impact.
tara-eng-runtime: plan: 1) route override to exclude header-key hashing for this tenant (canary to 10% nodes) 2) set prefix_cache.ttl=30s for that tenant 3) enable prefix-key-canonicalization on runtime (normalize list-like headers) as a medium-term fix 4) patch SDK docs to discourage flags-in-headers.
leo-cust-sre: repro steps I used locally: 
```
# hit same model with varying header flags to mimic their churn
for i in {1..500}; do 
  curl -s -H "x-feature-flags: f$RANDOM" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' >/dev/null &
done
```
I reproduced p95 jump and saw cache keys increase in /metrics prefix_key_cardinality.
mike-sre: good repro. also captured kv traces: `kv.get_latency_p95` aligned with the p95 spike.
ops-bot: flagged hosts with hot eviction loops: host-47, host-52, host-61. Eviction rate > 1200/s.
tara-eng-runtime: immediate steps I'll take: create route override (exclude noisy headers) + bump TTL to 30s for acme-corp buckets. I'll canary to 10% now. tagging @mike-sre to watch.
(4m later) deploy-bot: canary applied to 10% nodes.
mike-sre: watching metrics... kv_miss_rate down from 87% -> 42% on canary nodes. p95 on canary nodes from 900ms -> 260ms. good signal.
leo-cust-sre: customer reported partial improvement on our canary IPs. they still see some slow requests (from non-canary nodes).
tara-eng-runtime: rolling to 60% now. also enabling prefix-key-canonicalization experimental flag on canary to normalize comma-separated flags into sorted tokens.
anita-eng-ml: FYI, normalizing header ordering shouldn't affect model outputs since headers are metadata only. safe to enable.
(10m later) deploy-bot: override rolled to 100% on acme-corp route. prefix TTL updated. canonicalization enabled on 60% and being monitored.
mike-sre: on full rollout: kv_miss_rate now 9% cluster-wide for tenant; p95 stabilized ~140ms; cpu normalized. eviction loops stopped on flagged hosts.
leo-cust-sre: customer confirms p95 back to baseline. they still want permanent guardrails.
tara-eng-runtime: next actions — owner:tara: 1) add code path to ignore high-cardinality headers by default in route config (PR created) 2) add auto-splay warmup on new prefixes (stagger N initial warms) (RFC in progress) 3) add circuit-breaker: if prefix_cardinality growth > X%/min, temporarily route to no-cache fastpath.
jasmin-support: assigning followup ticket to eng-runtime: ENG-5821. customer update planned for EOD.
mike-sre: add alert: prefix_cardinality_delta > 2000 in 1m -> page oncall. set p95 regression detector tied to kv_miss_rate.
leo-cust-sre: thanks all — appreciated the fast triage. can you also share a minimal repro script I can give customer? the loop above works but it's noisy.
tara-eng-runtime: sure. will push a small reproducible harness gist and link in ENG-5821. gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kvcache-repro (private).
ops-bot: note: created incident INC-3489 -> status: mitigated, root cause: header-key cardinality explosion + aggressive eviction policy, resolution: route override + prefix TTL bump + canonicalization rollout.
jasmin-support: customer support message drafted and sent. :white_check_mark:
leo-cust-sre: closing loop — will reopen if anything pops up. great work. :tada:
